full_judgment:
In these two Rules arising out of two pre-emption cases between the same parties the common question is whether the deposit of the consideration amount as contemplated under sub-section 3(a) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act made though subsequent to the filing of the application but within the period of limitation as contemplated under sub-section (i) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act can be deemed to have been made at the time of making the application as such, in the present cases while filing the application for pre-emption no deposit of consideration money was male but it was done immediately thereafter and within the period of limitation. The courts below however rejected the claim of pre-emption only on the ground that the deposit of consideration money was not accompanied along with the application for pre-emption against which the present rules were obtained. 

 2. Clause (a) of sub-section (3) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act says that the deposit of the amount of consideration money or the value of the transferred holding shall be made in court at the time of making the application for pre-emption under sub-section (1) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It would, however, appear from sub-section (1) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act that an application for pre-emption may be made within 4 months of the service of notice upon the pre-empties or within 4 months from the knowledge of the alleged transfer under pre-emption. Thus, if an application for pre-emption is made within the period of limitation and the consideration money is also deposited in court within the period of limitation, in such circumstances it shall be deemed that the deposit of the consideration money has been made while making the application for pre-emption. In this connection it may he mentioned that it has not been said in clause (a) of sub-section (3) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act that the application for pre-emption shall be accompanied along with the deposit of consideration money or the value of the holding simultaneously. Clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 96 must be read along with the provision of limitation provided in sub-section (1) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. That being so, if the application for pre-emption and the deposit of consideration amount or the value of the transferred holding are made both within the period of limitation though separately, they shall he deemed and held to have been made validly within the given statutory period. 

 3. In the aforesaid circumstances, the decisions of the courts below dismissing the pre-emption cases on the ground that the deposit of consideration amount or the value of the transferred holding was made subsequent to the filing of the pre-emption cases though evidently both within the period of limitation suffers from clear error of law and such decisions are set aside. The Second Munsif of Gaibandha in the district of Rangpur is directed to re-hear Miscellaneous Case Nos. 192 and 193 of 1977 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and decide and dispose of the case on met it finally and expeditiously, These Rules are made absolute without any order as to costs.
